s1.quote: Mooring Pin 58 ft Max Depth 100 ft … The dive begins with a relatively easy yet thrilling swim-through leading directly onto the wall … the north wall is one of the best places on East End to spot turtles

mooring.value: Mooring buoy; mooring pin at 58 ft

highlights.text: Hawksbill and green turtles on the north wall

s1.quote: Mooring Pin 29 ft Max Depth 60 ft … The site features a pronounced ledge starting at 25 feet and dropping dramatically to 50 feet, with a rubble-strewn bottom

mooring.value: Mooring buoy; mooring pin at 29 ft

highlights.text: Ledge from 25 to 50 ft with rubble bottom
Coral outplanting site at eastern edge

s1.quote: Mooring Pin 33 ft Max Depth 60 ft … It is a labyrinth of swim-throughs, tunnels, caverns, crevasses, and arches

mooring.value: Mooring buoy; mooring pin at 33 ft

highlights.text: Cavern with tarpon and jacks hunting herring (summer)

s1.quote: Mooring Pin 40 ft Max Depth 60 ft … Maggie's Maze is distinguished by a long winding canyon that begins in the shallows … Nurse sharks love this area

mooring.value: Mooring buoy; mooring pin at 40 ft

highlights.text: Winding canyon ending in a swim-through

s1.quote: Easy Street Ranging in depth from 65 to 100 feet (20-30m) deep, this site features a swim-through as well as turtles and schools of fish
Orange Canyon - max depth 100 feet … named for the bright, beautiful and huge Elephant Ear sponges … As it is prone to current it cannot always be dived

s2.quote: Orange Canyon At 60 feet (18m) deep, a large coral head on the wall roughly marks a split of two canyons filled with orange elephant ear sponges as well as gorgonians and sea fans

highlights.text: Two canyons lined with orange elephant-ear sponges

hazards.text: Prone to current; cannot always be dived

summary.text: A spectacular wall site toward Northwest Point named for its big orange elephant-ear sponges, with two canyons split by a large coral head at about 60 ft. Current often makes it undiveable, so it is only done when conditions allow.

s1.quote: Bonnie’s Arch There’s plenty to see at this site between 40 and 70 feet (12-21m) deep … a large (50 foot / 15m) coral bridge / archway

s2.quote: Bonnie's Arch: Bonnie's Arch is a lovely dive site located right in front of the Northwest Point of Grand Cayman … The bottom of the arch is at a depth of 70 feet

highlights.text: Horse-eye jacks, turtles, tarpon and seahorses

summary.text: A scenic reef off Northwest Point centred on a curving natural coral arch roughly 50 ft across, with the base of the arch near 70 ft. Ridges and valleys around it hold sponges, angelfish, tarpon, horse-eye jacks and turtles.
